description:
We are Ctrl Shift Code! This is our second year participating in the NASA Space Apps Hackathon. We are a group of 8th graders passionate about coding, website development, and creating new ideas. We’re excited to work together, learn new skills, and build something we can be proud of.

Team Project Information Video:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AJXCWww-IrK8rv9lI2aHI1IiixrmuSy3/view?usp=drive_link
summary: We developed an interactive game called the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. The game introduces kids ages 7-12 to the challenges of building and maintaining a lunar or Martian outpost. Players take on the role of mission planners and make decisions about essential systems, including life support, radiation shielding, power, and food production. Each decision affects the outpost's resources and its ability to support your crew. Our project addresses the challenge by turning complex space exploration concepts into an interactive, hands-on learning experience. Instead of simply reading about space missions, players actively make decisions, solve problems, and see the results of their choices. This project is important because it makes STEM and space exploration more accessible to younger students while building critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
details: We developed an interactive game for young children that trains them to make challenging decisions when tough scenarios are presented to them. The game teaches kids to spend resources wisely and shows them how every decision affects another. The game works by letting the players plan their outpost/colony and resources, then they are presented with scenario-based questions where either decision will affect their outpost positively and negatively. This is important because it teaches young explorers the decision making part of space exploration and how they will need to use different strategies in times where quick thinking and action is needed. We used multiple softwares and NASA resources to build our website one of the softwares we used most was an app called Lovable that we used for the coding of our platform. When building out interactive game, we had to consider many things, such as how the game would keep younger audiences hooked and how to integrate data from NASA resources.
